title: Dow Slides as Yields Surge, Nvidia Plummets, Anthropic Targets IPO Price – Investor’s Business Daily
body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped Tuesday afternoon as Treasury yields surged following a hotter‑than‑expected inflation reading, while technology heavyweight Nvidia tumbled on profit‑taking pressure and AI‑focused startup Anthropic disclosed the price band for its upcoming initial public offering. The confluence of rising borrowing costs, mixed earnings signals and a high‑profile IPO has investors recalibrating risk appetites across the equity market.

The 10‑year Treasury yield jumped to 4.48%, its highest level in more than two years, after the Labor Department reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in June, outpacing economists’ median forecast of 0.4%. The unexpected uptick in core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy components, reinforced concerns that the Federal Reserve may keep interest rates elevated for longer than previously anticipated. Higher yields typically depress the valuation of growth‑oriented stocks, which rely heavily on discounted future cash flows, and the Dow’s 0.6% decline reflected that dynamic.

Technology shares felt the ripple effect most acutely. Nvidia, the chipmaker that has been the poster child for the AI boom, fell 4.2% after posting a modest revenue beat but seeing its gross margins compress amid rising input costs. The stock’s slide also signaled a broader rotation out of high‑flying AI plays that have surged more than 200% over the past twelve months. Analysts note that while demand for Nvidia’s GPUs remains robust, the market is beginning to price in a more measured growth trajectory as enterprises temper capital spending in the face of tighter financing conditions.

Adding to the market’s focus on the AI sector, Anthropic, the San Francisco‑based AI safety and research firm backed by major investors such as Google’s parent Alphabet, announced its IPO price range of $22 to $26 per share. The company is seeking to raise up to $1.5 billion, valuing it at roughly $5 billion post‑offer. The pricing band places Anthropic in line with other AI‑centric listings that have recently debuted, suggesting that investors are still willing to pay a premium for exposure to the next wave of generative‑AI technology. However, the modest upper limit relative to the lofty valuations seen earlier in the year hints at a more cautious appetite, likely driven by the same inflation‑driven rate concerns that are rattling the broader market.

Equity analysts point out that the current environment creates a dichotomy: while the macro backdrop is tightening, the AI narrative continues to attract capital. “We’re seeing a classic risk‑on/risk‑off tug‑of‑war,” said Maria Torres, senior strategist at Capital Edge. “The Fed’s stance on rates is the dominant driver for the next few weeks, but the AI theme remains a powerful catalyst that can offset some of the downside pressure, especially for companies that can demonstrate clear pathways to monetization.” 

The market’s reaction also underscores the importance of sector rotation. Defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples posted modest gains, buffering the overall index from a steeper decline. Meanwhile, financials, which benefit from higher rates, posted mixed results as banks weigh the upside of increased net interest margins against the risk of loan‑portfolio stress.

Looking ahead, traders will be watching the upcoming release of the Producer Price Index and the Federal Reserve’s policy statement for clues on whether the rate‑hiking cycle is truly nearing its end. A softer inflation print could revive confidence in growth stocks, potentially stabilizing Nvidia and other AI‑related equities. Conversely, if price pressures persist, the market may see further yield climbs, prompting additional pull‑backs in high‑valuation sectors. Anthropic’s IPO will serve as a barometer for investor appetite for AI exposure in a higher‑rate world, and its performance on debut could set the tone for the next wave of technology listings.
